clue.text: Courteous founders get stuff from elsewhere

indicators.note: a ship that founders collapses and sinks, so the letters of the preceding word break apart and are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Polite company founders buy in their supplies from other firms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'founders' looks like a noun (the people who start a firm) but it is a verb signalling that COURTEOUS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsource is to obtain goods or services from an outside supplier rather than produce them in-house.

clue.text: Arrogant in court, a matter of some regret

parts.note: someone up before the magistrate is appearing in court
a pity is something regrettable

explanation.surface: Being haughty in court is something to regret.
explanation.walkthrough: To be up, in British usage, is to be in court facing a charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppity is an informal word for self-important or presumptuous.

clue.text: Blind test

definitions.meaning: to check people for a disease or suitability

explanation.surface: A test done without looking, like a blind tasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen can be a shield like a window shade, and to screen is to examine or vet.

clue.text: Free one in French bar

parts.note: un is French for one
to bar a door is to lock it

explanation.surface: A single person released in a French bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlock something is to open it up and release it.

clue.text: Terrier, e.g., may drink from this — could a young person?

definitions.text: Terrier, e.g., may drink from this
definitions.note: a Terrier is a member of Britain's Territorial Army, a part-time soldier

parts.note: can expresses ability, as could does
a teen is a young person

explanation.surface: A dog drinks from a bowl, and so might a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrier' looks like a dog; it is a British Territorial Army reservist, who drinks from a soldier's flask.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a soldier's water flask, or a mess where troops eat and drink.

clue.text: Form of art flummoxing more minds

indicators.note: to flummox is to confuse, so the letters of the following words are muddled

explanation.surface: A style of art that baffles more and more people.
explanation.definitionFit: Modernism is the early twentieth-century movement that broke with traditional artistic forms.

clue.text: I instruct player in court well — right on gold

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: so, as in 'so, what now?', is a filler like well
licit means lawful, right
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A lawyer speaks: I brief the advocates, and I'm right on the money.
explanation.walkthrough: In British practice a solicitor instructs the barrister who performs in court.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is spoken by the answer itself: this kind of lawyer briefs the barrister who argues the case.

clue.text: 'Crossroads' for viewers? One leaves server near Slough

indicators.note: the two pieces are placed next to each other
the numeral for one departs from the word for a server

parts.note: a waiter serves at table
I is the Roman numeral one
to slough a skin is to shed it

explanation.surface: A soap called Crossroads plays to an audience near the town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossroads was a British TV soap; Slough is a town west of London. The watershed is the 9pm UK broadcasting turning point, after which adult content is allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A watershed is a turning point, and for television viewers it is the evening hour separating family viewing from adult programmes.

clue.text: The Crown's bottled export?

definitions.meaning: the Latin word for a crown, also used for the ring of light round the sun
a Mexican lager sold abroad in bottles

explanation.surface: It sounds like asking what the monarchy ships abroad in bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Corona is Latin for crown, and Corona is also a well-known Mexican beer exported in bottles.

clue.text: Pitch outside rec is not flat

indicators.note: one word stands outside the other, so the throw is wrapped around the recreation ground

parts.note: to pitch is to throw, which is to sling
a rec is a recreation ground, a park

explanation.surface: A sports pitch beside the recreation ground is not level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks like a playing field to go with 'rec', but here it is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparkling drink is fizzy, the opposite of a flat one that has lost its bubbles.

clue.text: Coppers (in disguise) in Welsh river wrap up

indicators.note: the plain-clothes police are placed within the river's name

parts.note: the Dee rises in Wales
the CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, are detectives who work in plain clothes

explanation.surface: Undercover police in a Welsh river bring their operation to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap up a matter is to settle or conclude it, as one does when making a final choice.

clue.text: Church in High Street, right place for wounded to lie

indicators.note: the church abbreviation sits inside the other letters
high means drunk, so the letters of the next word reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A church on the High Street is the right place for the wounded to lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High Street' reads as one familiar British phrase, but 'High' (drunk) is the anagram signal acting on the second word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher is a frame for carrying an injured person lying flat.

clue.text: Genesis reformed cutting English rock

indicators.note: the letters of the first book of the Bible are formed again in a new order
the English letter is cut away from that book's name before the rest is rearranged

explanation.surface: A reworked Book of Genesis with the English cut out sounds like a revised Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove an E from GENESIS and rearrange the remaining GNSEIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a coarse metamorphic rock with banded minerals.

clue.text: Busy oilworker perhaps gets one over panel

parts.note: to get one over on someone is to con them
a table is a flat slab or panel, as in an architectural panel

explanation.surface: An oil-rig worker gets the better of a review board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy' is British slang for a police officer, and an 'oilworker' is a painter in oils, here John Constable.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank of police officer called a busy in slang shares its name with the English landscape painter who worked in oils.

clue.text: Chap who can't afford a break desperately leaves card above

definitions.text: Chap who can't afford a break

indicators.note: in a down answer, the joker comes above the rearranged letters

parts.note: a card is a joker, a wag

indicators.note: acting desperately means wildly, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A man too poor for a holiday frantically leaves a card on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage slave is someone wholly dependent on a low salary, unable to take time off.

clue.text: Plant trees on each and every stop

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece rests on the second

parts.note: to forest land is to plant it with trees
all means each and every one

explanation.surface: An order to plant trees on every last stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to prevent something by acting first, to head it off.

clue.text: American, not heartless, that may be a soldier

indicators.note: with its heart gone, the middle letter of the word not is dropped, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: An American, not lacking feeling, who might be in the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the O from NOT, giving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldier ants are a caste of large-jawed insects that guard the colony.

clue.text: Climbing sport cut short here

indicators.note: in a down answer, climbing means the letters rise, read from bottom to top
the last letter is cut off the word

parts.note: to sport is to play

explanation.surface: Climbing as a sport is cut short in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the Y off PLAY; 'Climbing' turns PLA upward. 'here' points to where climbing happens, a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's 'here' is the place where climbing, the sport just named, is done: a high mountain.

clue.text: Pulling article from charger give it a whirl

indicators.note: pulling the article out means it is removed from the dish

parts.note: a charger is a large flat dish or tray
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Pulling a piece of kit from a battery charger to test it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charger' suggests a battery charger or a horse; it is an old word for a large serving dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To try is to have a go at something, to give it a whirl.

clue.text: Blessed with continued luck, winner's name is put here

definitions.meaning: enjoying a run of successes, a winning streak
a roll of honour is a list on which victors' names are recorded

explanation.surface: A lucky streak and the list where champions' names are inscribed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a streak of success and, literally, means listed on a roll of honour.

clue.text: Gent sent back fish dish

indicators.note: the polite form of address for a gentleman is sent backwards

parts.note: a gent is addressed as sir
sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A gentleman in a restaurant returns his fish course to the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rissole is a fried cake of minced meat or fish, served as a dish.

clue.text: Go on about this reward in greens?

indicators.note: turning about means the word for chattering on is read backwards

parts.note: to go on, talk endlessly, is to yap

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to keep talking about a prize on the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'greens' suggests golf or vegetables; here it is slang for money (from American greenbacks).
explanation.definitionFit: Pay is the money given as a wage or reward, and greens is slang for dollars or cash.

clue.text: Mean to maintain maturity

parts.note: to maintain an opinion is to aver it
age means maturity, being grown up

explanation.surface: An intention to keep up one's maturity.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean of a set of numbers is its arithmetic average.

clue.text: What's central to kebab? Wife's beset by whiffs from the east

indicators.note: the wife is surrounded by the bad smells
in an across clue, read from the east is right to left, so the smells word is read backwards

parts.note: whiffs are bad smells, reeks

explanation.surface: A wife is surrounded by smells drifting from an eastern kebab shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' turns REEKS into SKEER, and W goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A kebab's meat is threaded on a long pin through its middle, which is what the definition describes.

clue.text: Prompt tiny boy to overlook city

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece looks down over the second

parts.note: Tiny Tim is the boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Urging a small boy to ignore the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt and timely both mean happening at the right moment, without delay.

clue.text: Uneasy feeling due to model gulping most of coffee

indicators.note: the rearranged letters swallow the coffee
to model is to shape, so the letters are reshaped
the last letter is dropped

parts.note: java is slang for coffee

explanation.surface: A fashion model gulps coffee and feels a vague unease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a person drinking the coffee, but 'to model' is a verb meaning to shape, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Déjà vu is the unsettling sense of having lived through the present moment before.

clue.text: Host rising round mostly deft hero who's famously pious

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the trimmed adjective
in a down answer, rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a host, a great number, is a sea of people

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped

parts.note: deft means neat, skilful

explanation.surface: A host stands up to welcome a nimble, devout hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' suggests someone entertaining guests; here it means a multitude, as in a sea of faces.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil calls the Trojan hero of the Aeneid 'pius' throughout, for his devotion to gods, family and duty.

clue.text: What goes round could possibly be mere tripe

indicators.note: the words that follow might be turned into something else, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that what's going round could just be rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A perimeter is the boundary that encloses an area, going all the way round it.

clue.text: Distributes bulbs, the first couple being free

indicators.note: the first two letters are set free, removed from the bulbs' name

parts.note: shallots are small onion-like bulbs

explanation.surface: Someone hands out bulbs and gives the first two away for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out or assign portions, as in distributing allotment plots.

clue.text: Person making the running in UN, say, last of three shunned

indicators.note: the letter picked from the following word is avoided, left out of the diplomat's title

parts.note: a United Nations envoy is an example of a peacemaker

indicators.note: only the final letter of the number word is taken

explanation.surface: A frontrunner at the United Nations, perhaps, when the last of three candidates is ostracised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of three' is E, removed from PEACEMAKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacemaker in a race sets the speed for the others, making the running.

clue.text: Chirpy historian accepting article in Spanish

indicators.note: the historian takes in the Spanish article

parts.note: Livy was a Roman historian
el is the Spanish masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A cheerful historian takes on a piece written in Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Chirpy and lively are synonyms for cheerful and full of energy.

clue.text: Please do stay chez moi

definitions.meaning: a phrase granting permission, go ahead
chez moi is French for at my place, so this means be a visitor in my home

explanation.surface: A host's invitation to come and stay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for go ahead and, literally, an invitation to visit as someone's houseguest.
